title: Γεωγραφικά (Geographica)
shelf_note: Casaubon's 1587 commentary and castigations on Strabo; the page is the end of the Book XIV notes and the start of Book XV, as catalogued (display title).
structure_note: 22 printed backsteps / 26 repeats over 231 numbered pages; in a dense two-column commentary with 'PAG. 470'-style lemma references this is most likely misread page numerals, not a splice. 186 of 249 pages translated.

tr_errors.english: or suitors as it is said) Rather suitors <note>original: "mnēstēras"</note> is said by the poets, and in Eustathius also … suitors is written
tr_errors.problem: the note is about the epithet 'thigh-reared/thigh-sewn' of Dionysus (hence Pliny's 'born from the thigh of Jove'); the English turns it into 'suitors' and invents an 'original: mnēstēras' that is on neither the leaf nor the transcription

tr_errors.english: It should be read as Carpasia according to Ptolemy and Diodorus; for it is incorrectly written as Keronie in Diodorus.
tr_errors.problem: Casaubon's conjecture (Kerynia) is replaced by another Cypriot town name, Carpasia; a reader is told the wrong emendation

tr_errors.source: Greek lemmata throughout (e.g. ἀκρατίδαν γοῦν; Ἄορνον δέ τινα πέτραν … Arrianus, Ἀλλὰ δὲ ἡ Ἄορνος …; ἡ δ' ἄνυδρον πολλήν) Arrianus κατάστικτον vocat)
tr_errors.english: 'PAGE 473. as if an uneducated life'; 'a crest with faithful defeat … But Arrian in his book … and the theft'; 'and Arrian calls it a constitution'
tr_errors.problem: garbled Greek rendered as fluent but meaningless English with no mark of doubt; Arrian's quotation on Aornos is nonsense; 'PAG. 472' becomes 'PAGE 473'

tr_errors.source: Diodorus vero Meropidem simpliciter vocat lib. XIII.
tr_errors.english: Diodorus, however, simply calls it Meropis in Book 4

tr_errors.source: scripserunt VI M. oppidorum fuisse nullum Co minus, gentium IX
tr_errors.english: there was no town smaller than five thousand, and of nine nations
tr_errors.problem: Pliny's '5,000 towns, none smaller than Cos' garbled

tr_errors.english: and Hierapytna) In Pliny, this is Hierocepia
tr_errors.problem: lemma rendered as a different place (Hierapytna, in Crete)

other.note: <meta>continues from previous page: At the mountain pass of Amanus</meta> heads the English; nothing on this leaf supports it

book_verdict: The Latin of Casaubon's notes is read well and the English of the long prose notes is sound, but the Greek lemmata are garbled and the English fills them with confident nonsense, including an invented 'suitors / mnēstēras' gloss and a wrong emendation (Carpasia for Kerynia). Not fit to show a philologist.

title: [Greek: Peri Bion, Dogmaton kai apophthegmaton ton en philosophia eudokimesanton: biblia deka] De vitis, decretis & responsis celebrium philosophorum libri decem
shelf_note: Froben's 1533 Basel Greek editio princeps of Diogenes Laertius; the page is Book X, the Letter to Menoeceus.
structure_note: 899 page records against pages_count 600 (874 vs 568 translated): split into single pages but the book counts are stale.

ocr_errors.image: τοῦ μακαρίως ζῆν ἐστὶ τέλος
ocr_errors.problem: small slip

tr_errors.english: and the tranquility (ataraxia) of the soul
tr_errors.problem: this 1533 print (and the transcription) reads 'of the body'; the English silently substitutes the familiar 'of the soul' from the received text

tr_errors.source: ὅταν ἐκ τοῦ μὴ παρεῖναι τὴν ἡδονὴν ἀλγῶμεν. οὐκέτι τῆς ἡδονῆς δεόμεθα.
tr_errors.english: …when we feel pain because pleasure is absent. When we do not feel pain, we no longer need pleasure.
tr_errors.problem: the clause 'When we do not feel pain' is not on this leaf (it is missing in this edition); the English supplies it from the received text without marking it

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The English 'When we do not feel pain, we no longer need pleasure' and 'tranquility of the soul' come from the standard text of the Letter to Menoeceus; the leaf reads 'ἀλγῶμεν. οὐκέτι τῆς ἡδονῆς δεόμεθα' with no 'ὅταν δὲ μὴ ἀλγῶμεν', and 'τοῦ σώματος ἀταραξίαν'. Small and in the right direction, but not this edition's words.

book_verdict: Transcription is excellent and the English reads well, but the translation quietly follows the received text of Epicurus where this 1533 print differs (adds a missing clause, 'soul' for the printed 'body'); fine for a general reader, misleading for anyone studying this edition.

title: Philosophical Works
shelf_note: Catalogued as Psellos, 'Philosophical Works', date unknown, but this leaf is the crow-and-mouse chapter of Stephanites and Ichnelates (the Greek Kalila wa-Dimna), in a manuscript. It may be a miscellany that includes Psellos; the title doesn't say so.
structure_note: The image is an unsplit two-page manuscript opening (foliated 75 on the right) while the record says page 71; 32 backsteps in 107 numbered pages fits a mix of folio numbers and openings. The book is a Greek manuscript, not print.

book_verdict: Right opening, but the minuscule is read badly: 'partridge' is invented twice and the English adds a note claiming the manuscript says partridge; much of the rest is fluent English over garbled Greek. The catalogue (Psellos, Philosophical Works) doesn't match the Stephanites and Ichnelates text on this leaf.
